verdict.rationale: The IRS's own pages state the walls in front of each filing path before the user begins. Online account sign-in requires ID.me with selfie, video and biometric verification, and signed mobile-friendly forms such as the 83(b) Form 15620 require an Online Account. The EIN assistant publishes its hours, its 15-minute no-save session and its one-EIN-per-day limit. E-file provider enrollment publishes its fingerprinting step and its up-to-45-day approval clock. Missing for 10: a single consolidated pre-flight list of requirements per filing path, first-party detail of the exact ID.me proofing steps and documents, and independent or hands-on corroboration that no undisclosed walls appear mid-flow.

support.subject: As a founder, the service publishes exactly which account, credential, and identity-proofing steps stand between me and filing — stated before I start, not discovered mid-flow

citations.quote: You'll need an account with ID.me to sign in to access your tax information and use services on IRS.gov.
Online Account (OLA) is required to complete mobile friendly forms that require signatures
It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity, and you'll need to start over.
it can take up to 45 days from the date of submission for the IRS to approve your e-file application
You can apply for only 1 EIN per responsible party per day.
